correctness.rationale: For normalized two-ball monomials the exact map is a one-to-one orthogonal weighted shift with coefficient \(e^{-\epsilon u-\epsilon^a v}\) (u+v)/(u+v+k) times the stated factorial ratio, including the zero constant monomial. The coefficient is uniformly (v/(u+v))^{k/2}(1+O_k(1/v)) for \(v\ge1\). Fixed-v contributions are strictly lower order. Positive inner sums are within one of their monotone integrals; the resulting H_q Laplace integral has Gamma, logarithmic and finite-integral limits according to \(q=kp/2\). Riemann sums at v~epsilon^{-a} give exactly the three leading coefficients with negligible error \(O(\epsilon^{-a})\). The proof covers all quantified \(k\ge1\), fixed \(0<a<1\) and \(p>0\), and specifically excludes endpoints. A standalone checker passed 8712 exact rational norm and shift identities, plus finite partial sums, but the infinite statements rely on the written dominated-convergence proof rather than those finite checks.

value.rationale: This gives a natural full parameter-space inverse quantitative answer to how Schatten norms deteriorate when a new compact-range companion approaches a known noncompact operator anisotropically. The angular vanishing degree k and Schatten exponent p collapse to the meaningful threshold \(kp=2\), with different sharp divergence powers and a logarithmic critical boundary. Coefficients are exact and depend nontrivially on the time-scale separation \(0<a<1\). General compact-range membership theorems are qualitative; they do not give these sensitivity constants. This is mathematically motivated rather than an arbitrary small numerical calculation; the analytic reduction and proof cover infinitely many integer degrees and all positive exponents.
